title: Best Payroll Software Australia (2026): Guide & Top Picks
summary: Compare the best payroll software Australia offers (November 2026): pricing, STP Phase 2, Payday Super support, and top picks for every business size.
body_markdown:
This guide compares the best payroll software in Australia for 2026, covering Single Touch Payroll (STP) Phase 2 and the new Payday Super rules, so you can find a tool that keeps you compliant without the admin headache. Managing payroll in Australia can feel like a full time job, especially with compliance rules constantly evolving. Thankfully, the right payroll software can turn this complex task into a fast, automated process. Whether you’re hiring your first employee or managing a growing team, you’ll find a tool that fits here.


This guide breaks down everything you need to know about choosing the best **payroll software Australia** has to offer. For a broader market view, see our[best software for payroll guide](https://www.bolto.com/blog/best-software-for-payroll) . We’ll cover how it works, what to look for, and compare the top options on the market.


**TL;DR**


- STP Phase 2 reporting is a baseline requirement for Australian employers.
- From July 1, 2026, Payday Super generally requires employers in Australia to pay super alongside wages and calculate it on qualifying earnings.
- Xero or QuickBooks suit businesses already using those accounting tools, Employment Hero suits award heavy teams, and Payroller suits teams of 1 to 5.
- For hires outside Australia, an Employer of Record (EOR) or global HR system like Bolto covers payroll abroad.


## What Is Payroll Software?


At its core, **payroll software** is a digital tool that automates the entire process of paying your employees. This includes calculating wages, withholding the correct amount of tax, managing superannuation contributions, and keeping detailed records of every pay run. These systems are important for modern businesses because they drastically save time and reduce the risk of human error.


The shift to digital is undeniable. The adoption of cloud based solutions like online payroll systems has saved small businesses serious hours of admin time each month.[Single Touch Payroll (STP)](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/hiring-and-paying-your-workers/single-touch-payroll) reporting became mandatory for Australian employers back in July 2019 and remains a baseline requirement in 2026, so having reliable software is no longer a luxury, it’s a necessity. As a result, the market for **payroll software Australia** continues to grow as more businesses ditch manual spreadsheets for smarter, compliant tools.


## How Payroll Software Works in Australia


Australian payroll has its own unique set of rules, and good software is built to handle them automatically. Here are the key compliance areas your software needs to manage:


- **Single Touch Payroll (STP):** This is the big one. STP is the Australian Taxation Office’s (ATO) system for real time payroll reporting. In Australia, each time you pay your employees, STP compliant software generally sends a report to the ATO detailing wages, taxes, and super contributions. Modern systems are built to handle the latest STP Phase 2 rules, which require more detailed data reporting.
- **Superannuation Guarantee:** Your software must correctly calculate the superannuation guarantee for each eligible employee. As of November 2026, the super guarantee rate in Australia is generally 12%, the rate that has applied since July 1, 2025. Under the ATO's Payday Super changes starting July 1, 2026, super guarantee is generally calculated on qualifying earnings, which generally include ordinary time earnings plus amounts such as salary sacrificed super. Good software typically applies the current rate and earnings base automatically, but you should confirm details against current ATO guidance.
- **Modern Awards:** Australia has a complex system of modern awards that set out minimum pay rates and conditions for different industries. Quality payroll systems can interpret these complex award rates, including overtime and penalty rules, to help you pay people correctly.


Handling these rules manually is hard, and small STP or super mistakes can go unnoticed until the ATO follows up. The right **payroll software Australia** handles all these moving parts in one simple workflow.


## What Changed for Australian Payroll in 2026


Starting July 1, 2026, the Australian Taxation Office’s[Payday Super rules](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/super-for-employers/paying-super-on-payday/how-to-work-out-and-pay-super) generally require employers in Australia to pay superannuation guarantee at the same time as wages, instead of on the old quarterly schedule. Contributions are generally due to reach the employee’s fund within seven business days of payday, and super is generally calculated on qualifying earnings. This is general information, not legal advice, and rules can vary by situation and change over time, so check current ATO guidance or consult a qualified professional for your specific circumstances.


- Confirm your software can pay super every pay run instead of quarterly.
- Check that super is calculated on qualifying earnings for each employee.
- Make sure the system flags late or rejected super contributions so you can fix them quickly.


## The Key Benefits of Using Payroll Software


Adopting a quality payroll system offers some serious advantages that save you time, money, and headaches.


- **Fewer Errors and Costly Fines:** Automation cuts down on manual calculation mistakes, which can otherwise lead to underpayments, corrections, and penalties.
- **Built in Compliance:** Payroll rules change often, and keeping up manually can be a lot of work. Good software updates to reflect new tax rates and super rules, which can help you stay on top of your obligations without needing to be a legal expert.
- **Massive Time Savings:** Cloud based payroll systems automate calculations, tax filings, and payslip distribution, turning hours of manual work into minutes. This frees you up to focus on growing your business.
- **Enhanced Data Security:** Payroll data is highly sensitive. Storing it in spreadsheets is a major risk. Reputable providers use encryption and secure cloud storage to protect your data.
- **Employee Self Service:** Most modern systems include an employee portal where staff can view payslips, track leave balances, and submit timesheets. This empowers your team and reduces administrative queries for managers.
- **Accounting Integrations:** The best payroll tools connect with your accounting software, like Xero or QuickBooks. This cuts out double data entry and helps keep your financial records accurate and up to date.


## Choosing Payroll Software for Your Business Size


The right solution depends heavily on the size and complexity of your business.


### Payroll Software for Small Business


If you run a small business, you need a solution that is affordable, user friendly, and covers all your compliance basics. For adjacent tools you’ll likely need as you grow, check out our[HR software for small business guide](https://www.bolto.com/blog/hr-software-small-business-guide) . Simplicity is key, as payroll duties often fall to the owner or an office manager, not a dedicated HR professional.


Under Australian tax law, micro employers generally still report through STP and pay super for eligible employees. While free payroll apps exist for very small teams (for instance, some allow you to lodge STP for a single employee at no cost), it’s important to choose a reliable system. Payroll mistakes can result in ATO penalties.


Many small businesses start with the payroll module built into their accounting software. MYOB and Xero both offer payroll as part of, or as an add on to, their accounting plans, which is often a budget friendly starting point. Since plans change often, check current pricing on each vendor’s site before you decide. If you want HR and payroll together, see our list of[HRIS systems for small companies](https://www.bolto.com/blog/hris-systems-for-small-companies) .


### Payroll Software for Medium to Large Business


As your business grows, your payroll needs become more complex. Medium to large businesses should look for scalable solutions that can handle a larger workforce and integrate with other HR systems.


In Australia, payroll tax is a state and territory tax. If your total Australian wages exceed a state’s threshold (for example, NSW’s $1.2 million annual threshold as of November 2026), you generally pay state payroll tax. Thresholds and rates vary by state and change over time, so check with the relevant state revenue office for your specific circumstances. A capable system can handle these multi state calculations.


Tools like ELMO and Humanforce are designed for larger organizations. ELMO offers an all in one HR and payroll solution for mid sized businesses in Australia and New Zealand, while Humanforce is tailored for enterprises with large, shift based workforces.

### Xero Payroll


Xero is one of Australia’s most popular accounting tools, and its payroll module is a natural fit for the thousands of businesses already using it for bookkeeping.


- **Best for:** Small businesses that already use Xero for accounting.
- **Why it’s great:** Its user friendly design and tight accounting integration are its biggest strengths. Business owners and their accountants can collaborate in real time, and all payroll data flows directly into financial reports. Xero supports STP Phase 2 reporting and can automate superannuation payments.
- **Things to consider:** It’s most cost effective when bundled with a Xero accounting plan. For very complex award interpretations, a more specialized tool might be a better fit.


### Employment Hero Payroll


Employment Hero is an Australian HR system that combines payroll with a full suite of HR tools, from onboarding to performance management.


- **Best for:** Businesses wanting an all in one HR and payroll system with strong compliance automation.
- **Why it’s great:** Its standout feature is its library of built in modern awards, which automates the interpretation of complex pay rates and penalties. This is a massive advantage for industries like hospitality and retail. Employment Hero acquired KeyPay, the payroll engine behind its software, and retired the KeyPay brand in March 2023, so the product now runs as Employment Hero Payroll.
- **Things to consider:** It might be more than you need if you’re just looking for a simple payroll calculator. The real value comes from using its integrated HR features.


### KeyPay


KeyPay is a highly respected and powerful payroll engine known for its automation and compliance features. It was built in Australia to handle local payroll complexities, and since March 2023 it has operated under the Employment Hero brand as Employment Hero Payroll, though you’ll still see the KeyPay name in older reviews and accounting integrations.


- **Best for:** Small to medium businesses that need strong award automation and for accountants managing multiple clients. Compare more[payroll programs for accountants](https://www.bolto.com/blog/payroll-programs-for-accountants) if you run pay for several clients.
- **Why it’s great:** KeyPay excels at automatically applying correct award rates, penalties, and loadings, which removes a huge manual burden. It integrates smoothly with major accounting tools like Xero, MYOB, and QuickBooks.
- **Things to consider:** Now that it’s part of Employment Hero, it functions as the engine behind that system, but it remains a strong standalone choice for those who need pure payroll firepower without the full HR suite.


### QuickBooks Payroll Australia


QuickBooks Payroll is the integrated payroll solution within QuickBooks Online, tailored for the Australian market.


- **Best for:** Small businesses that use QuickBooks Online for their accounting and have straightforward payroll needs.
- **Why it’s great:** The built in integration is the main draw. All your payroll data automatically flows into your general ledger, saving time and preventing errors. It covers all the basics like pay as you go (PAYG) withholding, super, leave, and STP reporting effectively.
- **Things to consider:** Its capabilities for interpreting complex modern awards are more limited compared to specialized Australian providers. It’s perfect for standard salaried or hourly employees but may require manual workarounds for complex penalty rates.


### Payroller


Payroller has quickly become a favorite among micro businesses and sole traders thanks to its simplicity and attractive pricing.


- **Best for:** Very small businesses (1 to 5 employees) looking for a simple, free, or low cost mobile solution.
- **Why it’s great:** It’s a mobile first app that lets you run payroll, send payslips, and lodge STP reports directly from your phone. Its free plan for a single employee is a huge draw, and its paid plans are extremely affordable, costing just a few dollars per additional employee per month.
- **Things to consider:** It is not designed to scale. Once your team grows or your needs become more complex, you will likely need to migrate to a fuller featured system.

## Factoring in the Cost of Payroll Software in Australia


The cost of **payroll software Australia** varies, but there are options for every budget. Pricing is typically a flat monthly fee or a per employee per month model.


- **For micro businesses:** You can start for free. Payroller offers a free plan for very small teams, with low cost per employee paid plans as you add staff.
- **For small businesses:** Integrated accounting and payroll plans from MYOB and Xero offer good value, with pricing that depends on the plan tier and headcount.
- **For larger businesses:** Fuller featured systems like ELMO are usually quoted based on features and employee count, so costs scale with your organization.


When comparing prices, consider the value. A slightly more expensive system that saves you hours of admin time or prevents a single costly error can easily pay for itself.


## DIY Payroll vs. Using an Accountant


Do you need an accountant to run your payroll? Not necessarily. Modern **payroll software Australia** is designed to be user friendly enough for business owners to manage themselves.


However, accountants still play a key role. If you advise multiple clients, our[best payroll software for accountants](https://www.bolto.com/blog/best-payroll-software-for-accountants) guide can help you pick the right stack. Many businesses adopt a hybrid approach: they use software for the day to day pay runs, and consult their accountant for initial setup, end of year reconciliation, and complex situations. The collaborative nature of cloud tools like Xero makes this easy, as you and your accountant can access the same data in real time.


## Can You Do Payroll for Free?


Yes, it is possible to do payroll for free in Australia, especially if you have a very small team.


- **Freemium Apps:** Services like Payroller offer a free plan for one employee, which includes STP reporting and payslips. Another option, e PayDay FREEPAY, allows you to pay up to 3 employees for free.
- **Limitations:** Free software typically comes with limitations. You can expect minimal customer support and a lack of advanced features. These tools are a great starting point, but you should plan to upgrade to a paid solution as your business grows.


## Payroll Software Australia FAQs


### What should I look for when choosing payroll software in Australia?


Look for a system that is STP Phase 2 compliant, automates tax and superannuation calculations, and offers features like leave management and an employee self service portal. These core features help you keep up with your obligations in Australia and save you hours of admin time.


### Can payroll software manage leave and superannuation?


Yes, absolutely. Most modern systems track all types of leave, allow employees to submit requests, and automatically calculate superannuation on each payslip. They centralize many routine HR tasks.


### What’s the difference between standalone and integrated payroll software?


Integrated payroll is part of a larger accounting system like Xero or QuickBooks, which keeps all your financial data in one place. Standalone payroll software focuses solely on payroll and may offer more specialized features, but it will need to be connected to your accounting software.


### Is free payroll software good enough?


Free payroll software can be a great starting point for micro businesses with one or two employees. However, it often lacks advanced features and support. Think of it as a temporary solution before you graduate to a full featured, paid system that can grow with your business.


### What’s the best payroll software for startups with under 50 employees in Australia?


For most startups under 50 people, the best fit depends on your current stack. Xero Payroll or QuickBooks Payroll make sense if you already use that accounting software. Employment Hero is a strong choice if you need modern award interpretation and HR tools in one place. Payroller suits very small teams of 1 to 5 employees on a tight budget.


### Does payroll software in Australia support Payday Super?


From July 1, 2026, employers generally need to pay super alongside wages instead of quarterly. Most major tools, including Xero, Employment Hero, and QuickBooks, have been updating their systems to generally support paying super every pay run, though the details can vary by plan. Confirm the specifics with your vendor and check current ATO guidance before you rely on this for your own payroll.


### What AI tools help automate HR and payroll as a startup scales beyond Australia?

Many Australian startups keep local payroll software for domestic staff and use one global system for every hire abroad.
